It consists of two major parts: the striatum and the hippocampus. The striatum is clued into sensory inputs, like nearby landmarks. The hippocampus, meanwhile, constructs continuous, dynamic mental maps of your environment. It helps you figure out how to get somewhere, even if you've never been or haven't taken that exact route before.
